messages:
anya: Deploybot flagged a canary p95 and error bump after the v5.4.0 rollout (region: us-west). p95 ~950ms, SLO 300ms, canary traffic ~9%. Auto-revert suppressed due to release window. Need quick decision: pin + staged rollback, full rollback, or try mitigation?
mike: can we get a quick breakdown of what's changed in v5.4.0? last commit touched kernel selection and batch heuristics.
deploybot: [ALERT] canary_p95_and_errors (alert_id: cb-9992). metrics: p95=952ms, error_rate=1.9% (baseline 0.4%). auto-revert blocked by change-window.
anya: blast radius check? any reserved/dedicated customers on that slice?
ops-bot: route members: internal test tenants + one sandbox dedicated customer. no SLA routes.
mike: low blast. prefer pin+staged rollback of canary slice only so we don't disrupt the main rollout. keep the rest of traffic on v5.4.0.
san: what's the tradeoff if we allow deploybot to auto-revert for canary only? can we enable auto-revert scoped to the route?
anya: we don't have a per-route auto-revert toggle in prod without a quick safe config change. I'd rather do manual pin then run the rollback script for the slice.
mike: ok action plan: 1) pin canary route to previous stable v5.3.8, 2) run staged rollback for canary slice, 3) leave pin in place for 30m, 4) update release-notes + CS blurb. ready for exec?
anya: +1. mike, can you take pin? i'll prepare the rollback command.
mike: executing pin: `redwood route pin --route=canary --version=v5.3.8 --actor=mike`
deploybot: [ACTION] Route pin executed by mike at 4987654330. pinned version: v5.3.8.
mike: pin done. anya, ready for rollback when you say go.
anya: running staged rollback: ```./rollback-script --to=v5.3.8 --region=us-west --slice=canary --staged=true --drain-time=30s``` starting 21:14 UTC
deploybot: [ACTION] Rollback initiated by anya at 4987654342. staged rollback progress: stage1 40% -> stage2 75% -> stage3 100%. logs: "drain -> swap model -> warm evict/cache populate -> shift slice traffic"
anya: rollback finished. canary p95 back to ~285ms, errors down to 0.5%. monitoring for 20m.
ops-bot: applied temporary mitigation: canary max_batch_size lowered to 6 (was 12) for safety.
mike: i'll add a release-note line and tag the commit with #staged-rollback-4987654321. tess, can you prepare CS blurb for the sandbox tenant?
tess-cs: yep. draft: "We observed increased latency on a small canary slice after a recent deploy. We pinned and rolled back the canary slice to the previous stable version while we investigate. No customer data impacted. We'll follow up with a root-cause update." fine to send once times are confirmed.
anya: timestamps: pin at 4987654330, rollback start 4987654342, rollback complete 4987654355. mike, push the release-note commit.
mike: pushed: "Canary staged rollback to v5.3.8 due to p95 + error regression; mitigation applied (reduced batch size). Investigating kernel/batching interaction." tagged #staged-rollback-4987654321.
tess-cs: sent email to sandbox tenant and posted to #customer-ops with times and link to status doc.
anya: created ticket ENG-6001 "repro and mitigate v5.4.0 canary p95 spike - batch heuristics and kernel selection" assigned to eng-runtime + eng-ml.
ops-bot: monitoring check: 10m p95 stable at 270-300ms; error rate normal. recommend leaving pin for 30m then decide.
sam-englead: good call. prefer staged rollback over global revert here. follow-up: add a canary gating check for batch-size increases and an automated per-route autorevert feature backlog item.
anya: agreed. closing thread after 30m if no regression. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
